What is an LLM?

2
A new kind of resource:
general-purpose intelligence,
bought by the token
(kind of)
From outside, looking in
f : String -> String

Outside the API boundary, this is the observable behaviour.

No hidden state is carried between calls.

Nondeterministic

"What is spin?"

→

"Spin is..."

"Angular..."

"In QM..."

Same input, different outputs: the model samples from P(next token | context)

Temperature
P(token_i) = exp(ℓ_i/T) / Σ_j exp(ℓ_j/T)
0.1 · ground state3.0 · hot
The electron has

Direct analogy to the Boltzmann distribution. Low T freezes into the ground state; high T melts toward uniform.

Tokens

Not characters. Not words.

Subword chunks from a fixed vocabulary V of about 100k entries.

'theoretical physics' -> ['theor', 'etical', ' physics']

More precisely: f : Token* → Token*

An LLM is a stateless, nondeterministic function
f : String -> String
that samples from P(next_token | context)
via a single forward pass through a frozen neural network

One string in, one string out: the entire interaction

How chat works
Turn 1: [user_1] Turn 2: [user_1, asst_1, user_2] Turn 3: [user_1, asst_1, user_2, asst_2, user_3]

The client re-sends the entire history every turn: the LLM has no memory.

Interlude

Failure modes

3½
The failure zoo: architectural
Hallucination

No way to guarantee the fidelity of information stored in the weights, and what comes out is sampled, not looked up.

Training cutoff

The weights are frozen once training ends. No continual learning: recall of anything later is guesswork.

Nonzero error rate

Every token is drawn from a probability distribution. Prose tolerates that; deduction and code do not.

Context rot

Attention degrades as the window fills. In our experience quality starts to sag beyond roughly 30% usage.

Four consequences of the architecture, not four bugs.

The failure zoo: post-training
Hyperfixation (reward hacking)

Rewarded for visible completion: it deletes the failing test, hard-codes the answer, declares success.

Sycophancy

Raters prefer being agreed with. So it preferentially asserts the falsehoods you would quite like to be true.

Confident wrongness

Fluent, specific, real-shaped, false, and unhedged. Never ask a model to check its own output.

Semantic shift

It imports assumptions from a better-studied neighbour: Jordan algebras silently treated as C*-algebras.

These four are trained in, and they compound with each other.

These are architectural facts,
not mysteries
A frozen network generating tokens by sampling,
steered by whatever happens to occupy its context.
And each one admits a structural countermeasure.
There is a way to correct for these errors
Reliable computation out of unreliable components.
This room has done that before.

The radical unlock versus chat

Errors compound

A flat chain of thought has no error detection. If each step succeeds with probability 1 − ε:

P(the whole derivation) = (1 − ε)ⁿ
per-step error
1%
steps
100
survive intact
37%

A slip at step 3 propagates silently to step 40, while the trace stays locally fluent throughout.

This is why long unchecked derivations rot

Three ways to spend compute on reliability
(a) flat chain. One slip at step 3; everything after it is quietly wrong.
(b) parallel repetition. Majority vote over final answers. Helps, but scales poorly with depth.
(c) recursive decomposition. Verify each block in isolation; expand the one that fails.

(c) is the concatenated-code strategy (von Neumann, 1956).

Above the verification threshold, reliability compounds instead of decaying

Why structure a proof?

Most proofs in physics are written as flowing prose:

“By linearity … and therefore … which contradicts … hence the result follows.”

This works well enough when the proof is short. But even a five-line argument can hide a gap, one that only surfaces when someone pushes back on a specific step.

And then the reader is left asking: which step was wrong?

Lamport structured proofs
1
the claim
1.1
ASSUME …
1.2
…
[1.1]
1.2.1
…
1.3
QED
[1.2]

Every assertion gets a hierarchical number: 1, 1.1, 1.1.1 …

Every step is justified: by citing earlier steps, or by its own children.

ASSUME / CASE / QED open and close scopes.

A leaf with no justification is an exposed gap.

Auditable

“I don't believe 1.3.2”

Modular

sub-steps refine independently

Gap-visible

nowhere for a hole to hide

That is the entire formalism: no logic syntax to learn

No-cloning, structured
1
There is no unitary U with U|ψ⟩|0⟩ = |ψ⟩|ψ⟩ for every state |ψ⟩.
1.1
ASSUME such a cloning unitary U exists.
1.2
Basis states clone: U|0⟩|0⟩ = |00⟩ and U|1⟩|0⟩ = |11⟩.
[1.1]
1.3
By linearity: U|+⟩|0⟩ = (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2.
[1.2]
1.4
By cloning: U|+⟩|0⟩ = |+⟩|+⟩ = ½(|00⟩ + |01⟩ + |10⟩ + |11⟩).
[1.1]
1.5
Contradiction: Schmidt rank 2 ≠ 1 , entangled on the left, product on the right.
[1.3, 1.4]
1.6
QED  The assumption 1.1 is false: no such U exists.
[1.5]

Doubt step 1.5? Expand it: the proof refines exactly where the sceptic pushes.

1.5.1
Arrange the four coefficients as a 2×2 matrix.
1.5.2
Its rank is 2 on the left, 1 on the right.

Each numbered step is the small, independently checkable block the error-correction recipe demands.

A hallucinated proof has nowhere to hide

github.com/tobiasosborne/vibefeld

Vibefeld: how trust accumulates

Provers propose, verifiers attack: a claim is accepted only when every challenge is resolved.

Every proposal, challenge, and resolution lands in an append-only ledger: a full audit trail.

Assumptions stay visible: an admitted claim taints everything that depends on it.

Provers convince. Verifiers attack. Truth emerges.

Break the correlations

A verifier only helps if its blind spots are not the prover's blind spots. Three knobs:

Blind the verifier

It sees the numbered artifact only, never the prover's reasoning.

Change model family

Claude checks GPT. Different labs, different training data, different failure modes.

Change capability class

A frontier model audits the output of a cheaper, faster one.

A blind spot shared by every fresh session of one model is often glaring to another

Agent harnesses are ordinary command-line programs: one agent invokes another through its shell tool, so this automates.

Defense in depth

Formalisation is not a single act. It is a spectrum of artifacts, increasing in cost and in rigour:

One-shot prose
a proof, as usual
→
Lamport tree
numbered, justified steps
→
Lemma DAG
explicit contracts between lemmas
→
Machine-checked
a kernel has the final word

No single layer is trustworthy alone. But the layers fail in different places: compose them. Swiss cheese (Reason, 2000).

An agent produces every layer almost for free

The single point of failure

Code has compilers. Proofs have proof assistants.

Planning documents have nothing.

You can verify that code implements a spec.

You cannot verify that the spec addresses the right problem.

The scarce resource is structural taste: knowing which problems are load-bearing and which are decorative

How trust is actually built

Trust is not granted; it is verified into existence.

The foundation is ground truth: primary sources, raw data, the actual output.

The masters of this: investigative journalists. every claim traced to a source, checked independently.

Cultivate the investigative mindset

Every layer we built today has failure modes
Context rot, hallucination, tool misuse, prompt fragility
The human in the loop is not optional
You can outsource cognition
but you can't outsource understanding

“545% cost-profit ratio”

Leaked P&Ls agree: Anthropic gross margin −94% (2024) → mid-60s% (Q1 2026), first operating profit Q2 2026; OpenAI 28% → 43% while free users consume ~half the inference bill

“We're profitable on inference.” (Altman, Aug 2025)    “>50%” (Amodei, Feb 2026)

The honest fine print

Subscriptions: the median $20 subscriber costs cents per month; <5% hit rate caps
$100–200 power tiers are bimodal (Altman, Jan 2025: Pro lost money), and rate limits cap the tail

What survives on the skeptic side:
long-context cost floors · reasoning models burn 10–50x tokens per query · GPU rents rose in 2026

The losses are real, but discretionary:
OpenAI 2025 operating loss ~$21B = R&D $19B + training ~$8B, on positive serving margins

Not failing to make money: choosing to reinvest more than they earn
